subject: Private deployment readiness — technical asks, timeline constraints, and exception lane
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cloudbridge.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment — initial readiness questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. CloudBridge is keen to move forward with a Private (VPC) deployment for our analytics workloads, but we need a short feasibility check across three areas before we commit to a pilot:

1) Network topology constraints — CloudBridge will enforce egress restrictions and a transit gateway pattern; we need to understand required ports, NAT/egress, and any persistent outbound connections from Redwood components.
2) Audit and evidence — we need to know what evidence and timeline you can provide for SOC2/audit artifacts and KMS access patterns.
3) Staff model — what on-call/Ops ownership do you expect on our side vs Redwood-managed duties during the pilot?

Can you put us in touch with the right technical and product owners and, ideally, a short mutual action plan? We are targeting an internal procurement decision by 2028-04-05.

Best,
Elena
Director of Cloud Platform
CloudBridge Solutions

Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment — initial readiness questions

Quick technical triage:

- Network: Redwood's private control plane in VPC mode initiates outbound connections to our control endpoints for heartbeats and metrics; these are TLS over 443 to specific CIDR ranges. For an outbound-restricted environment we can offer a proxied egress path (static IPs via NAT gateway) and support a whitelist of 8 IPs. No persistent inbound ports required for model serving; customer traffic terminates in their VPC to dedicated nat/elb endpoints.

- KMS: We support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS/HSM) — we need a brief access policy to validate envelope encryption flows. Key rotation is supported but will require a short maintenance window for rolling keys across hosts.

- Audit artifacts: We can produce runbook extracts, configuration snapshots, and token-level logs for the pilot. Full SOC2 package is not auto-generated; we can provide the artifact list and estimated delivery times.

Blockers / exceptions: If they require zero egress (air-gapped), that's a separate on-prem package and will push timelines + staff requirements. If they insist on dedicated HSM appliances on-prem, that is an exception that requires infra procurement and a 6–8 week lead time.

I'll draft the tech section of the MAP and a concise list of required network rules.

- Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer

From product/roadmap perspective:

- Pilot scope: we should limit the initial pilot to model serving (inference only) + audit log delivery; exclude advanced features (function calling, streaming exports) until pilot proves stability.
- SLA: for a pilot we can offer 99.5% availability and a best-effort latency target; anything higher requires Dedicated contract.
- Timeline: if we keep to basic scope and accept the proxied egress approach, we can stand up the pilot in ~3 weeks (env prep + smoke tests + audit checklist). If CloudBridge requires on-prem HSM or air-gap, move to 8–12 weeks.

I recommend we propose two MAP tracks: Standard (proxied egress, 3 weeks) and Exception (HSM/air-gap, 8–12 weeks) and ask CloudBridge to confirm which path they need.

-Marissa
Senior Product Manager
Redwood Inference

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment — initial readiness questions

Staffing/resourcing note:

- Ops coverage: For Standard track, we require 0.2 FTE from our infra team for onboarding + 0.1 FTE on-call during pilot weeks (rotational). Customer must provide a networking engineer point-of-contact for NAT/gateway changes and an IAM owner for KMS policy approvals.
- If CloudBridge chooses the Exception track (HSM/on-prem), we will need a dedicated infra engineer on-site/remote for 4 weeks during provisioning (estimate 0.6 FTE) and additional security engineering time for product adjustments.
- Cost: I'll draft an estimate in the mapping workbook; expect a non-recurring setup fee for the Exception track to cover engineering and validation time.

I'll update the redwood-private-mapping.xlsx with owners and the rough FTE math.

-Dylan
Director, Platform Ops
